# Goal: Determine which tickets met their first-response SLA.
# First, we find the earliest 'agent_response' event per ticket after its opened_at.
# Then, join to tickets to get first_response_minutes (difference between first agent_response and opened_at in minutes)
# Join policy with tickets to get the SLA first_response_minutes threshold.
# Determine if ticket's first response minutes <= policy threshold to mark SLA met.
# Finally calculate share of tickets meeting SLA.

query_first_response = """
WITH first_agent_response AS (
    SELECT
        te.ticket_id,
        MIN(te.event_at) AS first_response_time
    FROM ticket_events te
    JOIN tickets t ON t.ticket_id = te.ticket_id
    WHERE te.event_type = 'agent_response'
    AND te.event_at >= t.opened_at
    GROUP BY te.ticket_id
),
ticket_response AS (
    SELECT
        t.ticket_id,
        t.opened_at,
        far.first_response_time,
        JULIANDAY(far.first_response_time) - JULIANDAY(t.opened_at) AS response_days,
        (JULIANDAY(far.first_response_time) - JULIANDAY(t.opened_at)) * 24 * 60 AS first_response_minutes,
        t.policy_id
    FROM tickets t
    LEFT JOIN first_agent_response far ON t.ticket_id = far.ticket_id
),
sla_check AS (
    SELECT
        tr.ticket_id,
        tr.first_response_minutes,
        sp.first_response_minutes AS sla_minutes,
        CASE WHEN tr.first_response_minutes IS NOT NULL AND tr.first_response_minutes <= sp.first_response_minutes THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS sla_met,

)
